item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00287","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C01","C25","C09"],"selected_candidate_label":"C01","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C01 provides a concrete, material drafting template for the child: both use the same two-recital structure for an existing labor dispute that has resulted in a strike imperiling national safety, followed by the identical Title II powers clause, section 206 reporting requirement with a substituted deadline, and continuation-until-termination provision. C25 and C09 share the same administrative machinery, but their alternative formulations concerning threatened strikes and national health or safety are less exact.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"WHEREAS there exists a labor dispute at the plant of the American Locomotive Company ...; and WHEREAS in my opinion such dispute has resulted in a strike affecting a substantial part of an industry engaged in trade or commerce among the several States or with foreign nations, or in the production of goods for commerce, which strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national safety","parent_excerpt":"WHEREAS there exists a labor dispute between coal operators ...; and WHEREAS in my opinion such dispute has resulted in a strike affecting a substantial part of the bituminous coal industry, an industry engaged in trade and commerce among the several states and with foreign nations, and in the production of goods for commerce, which strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national health and safety","explanation":"The child closely adapts C01's factual recitals and operative statutory predicate, changing the parties and industry while retaining the realized-strike and continuation language."},{"child_excerpt":"The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with the provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before December 10, 1952.","parent_excerpt":"The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before April 5, 1948.","explanation":"The operative board-powers and reporting provisions are essentially verbatim, with only the reporting deadline changed."},{"child_excerpt":"Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.","parent_excerpt":"Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.","explanation":"The concluding provision is verbatim and preserves the same administrative machinery."}]}
